# fencing-bout-wallclock-program-standard

| | |
|---|---|
| Benchmark | Embodied Agent Olympiad |
| Mode | standard (`eai-standard-realtime/1.0`) |
| Twin | — (standard only: Olympiad sports have no privileged twin) |
| Simulator / robot | `mujoco` / `franka_panda` |
| Family / instance | `fencing_bout` |
| Oracle | `full` — solution/: the sport's reference player (camera images and /spec only); tools/check runs it live and it wins the default configuration |
| Agent time budget | 7200 s; tokens: protocol default (PROTOCOL §5) |

## Task
Two identical Franka Panda arms (held to the real robot's joint velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque and torque-rate limits), each on a 0.90 m pedestal on a cart running on a rail (a Festo EGC-TB-185 axis held to 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2 and 150 m/s^3) along a regulation 14 m piste and holding an epee (0.90 m blade, 13.5 cm bell guard), fence one FIE pool bout (5 touches or 3 minutes, no draws; one minute without a touch is unwillingness to fight, FIE t.124) in MuJoCo; blades, guards and bodies collide physically and the electric apparatus is modelled on the point's force along the blade; format bout: you against a scripted fencer (levels 1-3, `game spec` opponent_level), format duel: two players; format `bout` (seats A),
action level `high`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/fencing/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions).

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [FIE Technical Rules (t.) and Material Rules (m.), epee](https://static.fie.org/uploads/40/204126-Technical%20rules%20August%202026%20ang.pdf) version August 2026 |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | t.28, t.33, t.35 | footwork is a cart on a rail along the piste's centre line: no lateral boundaries and no passing |
| D2 | t.91, m.19, Material Rules Annexe B | the robot's whole structure (cart, pedestal, arm) is the target; the apparatus measures the force on the point along the blade (> 7.35 N for >= 2 ms, three consecutive 1 ms samples; lockout 45 ms, inside the 40-50 ms tolerance) |
| D3 | t.24, t.25 | corps-a-corps needs a trunk (cart, pedestal, shoulder) in contact with the other robot; arm-on-arm and blade contact is fencing at close quarters and goes on |
| D4 | t.31, t.32 | after a corps-a-corps both fencers move back equally (t.31 instead of t.32) |
| D5 | t.158-t.170 | no cards or penalties (the robots cannot commit the faults they punish), except the P-cards for unwillingness to fight (t.124, D9) |
| D6 | t.38 (competition formula) | one pool bout instead of a competition |
| D7 | - | the arms are Franka Panda arms held to the manufacturer's joint limits (velocity 2.175 / 2.61 rad/s, acceleration 7.5-20 rad/s^2, jerk 3750-10000 rad/s^3, torque 87 / 12 N m, torque rate 1000 N m/s; Franka 'Control Interface Specification and Robot Limits', FER): a full extension from on guard takes 0.55-0.75 s, slower against the footwork than a fencer's arm (fencing-2 used 1.5 x the velocity and acceleration limits: 0.50-0.58 s) |
| D8 | - | the footwork rail is a Festo EGC-TB-185 toothed-belt axis (catalogue: 5 m/s, 50 m/s^2, feed force 2500 N; Festo operating instructions 8162896, 2023-05) run inside that envelope: 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2, a jerk limit of 150 m/s^3 (an estimate: Festo publishes no jerk limit; the B9 feasibility study's value) and a motor force of at most 2500 N (fencing-4; up to fencing-3 the rail was no real product: 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2, 3000 N, no jerk limit). A 4 m advance at full speed takes about 2.6 s |
| D9 | t.124, t.170 (0.5) | unwillingness to fight (FIE Technical Rules, August 2026, t.124: 'There is unwillingness to fight when there is one minute of fencing without a hit'; the FIE applies its sanctions to direct-elimination bouts (t.124.1) and team matches (t.124.2), not to pool bouts) applies to our one pool bout, with the direct-elimination sanctions: one minute of fencing time, measured on the bout clock (`fencing_time_s`, effective fencing time as in t.37: 60 s = 6000 control steps of 10 ms; the wall clock takes slowdown x 60 s), without a hit -> 'Halt!'; the first time a P-red card to both fencers, a penalty hit each, both put on guard on the on-guard lines (t.124.1.a, t.22.6); the second time the P-black card to the fencer with the lower score, who loses the bout, at equal scores to the fencer who loses a seeded lot (t.124.1.b.i: lots for fencers not in the FIE ranking, as all of ours); no P-card at 4-4, the pool's 14-14 (t.124.3.a): the halt is called and the minute restarts; the minute restarts after each hit, double, annulled double, rear-limit hit (t.34) and penalty hit (t.124.3.d), not after a corps-a-corps; t.124 does not apply in the extra minute (t.124.3.f). fencing-5; up to fencing-4 a bout could be run out without a hit to the 3 minutes and the extra minute's lot |
